mechanism: Branching-adaptive shallow curvature: level 1 of an otherwise unchanged RQ-VAE is assigned in a Poincare ball of curvature kappa = -1/R^2 (radius R), with per-item radial coordinates fixed by a frozen behaviour statistic, while levels 2..L stay exactly baseline Euclidean. Once, from the Stage-2 TRAINING split, directed pair counts n_ij, M = Sum n_ij and ONE item-count vector f_i = Sum_j n_ij are formed; the idea's S_i = { j : n_ij > n_i n_j / M } is evaluated with that single vector at both indices (n_i = n_j = f_i), strictly, with no j != i guard, and s_i = |S_i|, T_i = log(1+s_i), b_bar = mean_i s_i, T_bar = mean_i T_i, R = max(1, log(N_items)/log(1+max(b_bar,1.1))), kappa = -1/R^2, T_max = 2R atanh(0.95) are cached and frozen. Per step, level 1 only: zhat = z/max(||z||,eps); t_i = T_i (or T_bar when USE_BEHAV is off); r_i = R tanh(min(t_i,T_max)/(2R)); u_i = r_i zhat_i; rho_k = R tanh(||e_k||/(2R)); c_k = rho_k e_k/max(||e_k||,eps); the artefact's literal quantity is d_ik = arccosh(1 + 2R^2||u_i-c_k||^2/((R^2-||u_i||^2)(R^2-||c_k||^2))), and the implementation multiplies it by the positive item-independent factor R, so d_ik = R*arccosh(...); the idea's max(...,1e-6 R^4) floor is NOT implemented and the floor case is mapped to +inf. k1 = argmin_k d_ik, z_q1 = e_{k1} (Euclidean row), res_1 = z - z_q1 with the baseline straight-through unchanged, levels 2..L run the plain Euclidean argmin, the loss is the baseline RQ-VAE reconstruction + codebook + commitment loss verbatim, and AdamW with the baseline schedule trains it. The geometry contract's projection is deliberately omitted for BOTH u_i (r_i <= 0.95R) and c_k (which may approach ||c_k|| -> R, where d_ik = +inf is the intended consequence and the argmin never selects such a code).

computations.name: directed_pair_counts
computations.definition: n_ij = #{(a,b) : a = i at position t and b = j at position t+1 of one Stage-2 TRAINING-split sequence of a training user}; f_i = Sum_j n_ij (the single item-count vector); M = Sum_{i,j} n_ij; N_items = 24556
inputs: Stage-2 TRAINING split sequences (training users only)
computations.output: sparse integer n_ij, the single count vector f (used as n_i and as n_j), scalar M, N_items
computations.note: Computed once, frozen before the first training step; validation/test sequences never enter. No j != i guard is stated, so whatever the counter emits is counted. The idea defines one item-count vector; the same vector f is indexed at i and at j, and no separate in-degree marginal is introduced (no sign-off for an out/in split was obtained).

computations.name: adjusted_successor_set
computations.definition: S_i = { j : n_ij > n_i * n_j / M } with n_i = n_j = f_i (one vector at both indices); s_i = |S_i|
computations.note: Strict inequality; equality with the popularity-only expectation is not an adjusted successor. This is the behaviour entry point; s_i propagates into T_i, b_bar, R and every radius.

computations.name: behaviour_scalar
computations.definition: T_i = log(1+s_i); b_bar = (1/N_items) Sum_i s_i; T_bar = (1/N_items) Sum_i T_i
computations.note: Cached as float32 with the USE_BEHAV flag and frozen before the first step; s_i = 0 gives T_i = 0 and a z-independent level-1 token for that item.

computations.name: curvature_constants
computations.definition: R = max(1, log(N_items)/log(1+max(b_bar,1.1))); kappa = -1/R^2; c = 1/R^2; T_max = 2*R*atanh(0.95)
computations.note: R is one global frozen scalar; the contract ball is c||x||^2 < 1 with radius 1/sqrt(c) = R. The 1.1 inner floor keeps the logarithm base above 1 and the outer max keeps R >= 1.

computations.name: item_radius_table
computations.definition: t_i = T_bar if USE_BEHAV is False else T_i; r_i = R*tanh(min(t_i,T_max)/(2*R))
computations.note: Load-bearing clamp: tanh(T_max/(2R)) = 0.95, so r_i <= 0.95R < R and R^2 - ||u_i||^2 >= 0.0975 R^2 > 0. Frozen constant; the lookup by item_id carries no gradient.

computations.name: item_ball_embedding
computations.definition: zhat_i = z_i / max(||z_i||_2, eps); u_i = r_i * zhat_i
computations.note: Smooth in zhat but evaluated with no gradient in this mechanism: u_i is consumed only by d_ik, which only feeds the argmin (see gradient_rules). eps is the baseline norm floor (1e-8); no projection is applied, and none is needed because r_i <= 0.95R < R.

computations.name: codebook_ball_embedding
computations.definition: rho_k = R*tanh(||e_k||_2/(2*R)); c_k = rho_k * e_k / max(||e_k||_2, eps)
computations.output: rho_k (256,), c_k (256 x 32) with ||c_k|| = rho_k < R
computations.note: E1 is not reparameterised: only the distance uses c_k, the reconstruction subtracts e_k. No projection is applied; ||e_k|| is unbounded, so ||c_k|| may approach R (for ||e_k|| >~ 20R, rho_k is indistinguishable from R in float64) and the resulting d_ik = +inf is intended (see level1_distance).

computations.name: level1_distance
computations.definition: arg = 1 + 2*R^2*||u_i - c_k||_2^2 / ((R^2 - ||u_i||_2^2)*(R^2 - ||c_k||_2^2)); d_ik = R * arccosh(arg); the denominator has NO max(., 1e-6*R^4) floor, and den <= 0 maps to d_ik = +inf
computations.note: Two explicit deviations from the idea as written, both argmin-purposed: (1) the idea's Eq. (4) returns arccosh(arg) alone; the implementation returns R*arccosh(arg), a positive item-independent rescaling that leaves the argmin unchanged and is what makes d_c(0,u_i) = 2R*atanh(r_i/R) = min(t_i,T_max) and the flat limit below equal 2||u-c||; (2) the idea's floor max(den, 1e-6 R^4) is removed, and the floor case is mapped to +inf, exactly as the continuous_surface does. The floor's job is done by the radius clamp: r_i <= 0.95R gives R^2 - ||u_i||^2 >= 0.0975 R^2, so the floor is only reachable via ||c_k|| -> R, which is the +inf case. The distance is consumed only by the argmin and is detached.

computations.name: level1_assignment
computations.definition: k1 = argmin_{k=1..256} d_ik (ties to the smallest index); z_q1 = e_{k1} = E1[k1]
computations.note: The one argmin and only coupling point: behaviour fixes r_i, curvature fixes what that radius means in angle, and the distance decides the token. No gradient, no relaxation, no entropy, no commitment, no Sinkhorn.

computations.name: level1_straight_through
computations.output: z_st (B x 32), forward value z_q1, identity Jacobian in z_i

computations.name: level1_residual
computations.note: Baseline residual formula; e_{k1} is a graph constant, so d res_1/d z_i = I. No lifting or normalisation is applied to res_1.

computations.name: deep_level_assignment
computations.definition: for l = 2..L: k_l = argmin_k ||res_{l-1} - e^{(l)}_k||_2; res_l = res_{l-1} - e^{(l)}_{k_l}
computations.note: Exactly baseline: Euclidean argmin per level, no curvature, no radius, no Sinkhorn, no temperature, no interface change; input is res_1 as before.

computations.name: reconstruction
computations.definition: z_hat = z_st + Sum_{l=2..L} sg(e^{(l)}_{k_l}); x_hat = decoder(z_hat)
computations.note: Forward value equals the sum of the selected Euclidean code vectors, as baseline; decoder shape, semantics and Stage-3 input format unchanged.

computations.name: baseline_loss
computations.definition: L = L_recon(x, decoder(z_hat)) + Sum_{l=1..L} ||sg(res_{l-1}) - e^{(l)}_{k_l}||_2^2 + beta * Sum_{l=1..L} ||res_{l-1} - sg(e^{(l)}_{k_l})||_2^2, with res_0 = z_i
computations.note: The baseline RQ-VAE reconstruction + codebook + commitment objective, unmodified; no behaviour/curvature/radius term, no extra hyperparameter, no temperature, no clip bound, no Sinkhorn.

computations.name: encoder_gradient_path
computations.definition: dL/dz_i = dL/dres_1 + 2*beta*(z_i - sg(e_{k1})) + Sum_{l=2..L} 2*beta*(res_{l-1} - sg(e^{(l)}_{k_l})) * (d res_{l-1}/d z_i), with d res_{l-1}/d z_i = I; exactly zero into R, kappa, T_max, r_i, rho_k, s_i, T_i, b_bar, T_bar and n_ij, f, M
computations.note: Three contributions: the reconstruction path delivered to res_1 (identity, since res_1 = z_i - e_{k1} with e_{k1} constant), the level-1 commitment term 2*beta*(z_i - sg(e_{k1})) from res_0 = z_i, and the deeper commitment terms chained back with identity Jacobians. Nothing flows through k1, d_ik, u_i, c_k, r_i, R, kappa, T_max or the frozen tables.

computations.name: switch_use_behav
computations.definition: t_i = T_bar if USE_BEHAV is False else T_i, consumed only by item_radius_table
computations.note: With USE_BEHAV=False every item sits at the single radius R*tanh(min(T_bar,T_max)/(2R)) and the assignment becomes a common-radius, item-independent metric d_ik = d_c(u,c_k) with no per-item branching resolution. It is not purely angular: with a common radius the distance still depends on ||c_k|| and, through the eps guard in zhat, on ||z||. R, kappa and T_max are untouched; one flag, not trained.

computations.name: switch_use_curv
computations.definition: USE_CURV=False: u_i = t_i*zhat_i, c_k = ||e_k||_2*e_k/max(||e_k||_2,eps), d_ik = ||u_i - c_k||_2; USE_CURV=True: the three formulas above
computations.note: USE_CURV=False IS the kappa->0 limit of the same block: r_i = R tanh(t_i/(2R)) -> t_i/2 and rho_k = R tanh(||e_k||/(2R)) -> ||e_k||/2, so R*arccosh(...) -> 2||(t_i/2)zhat_i - (||e_k||/2)ehat_k|| = ||t_i zhat_i - ||e_k||_2 ehat_k|| = ||u_i - c_k||, exactly, with constant 1 and no residual R/2. The common factor 1/2 hits item and codeword radius alike, which is why the argmin is unchanged; the T_max clamp is a curvature-only artefact and is dropped in this branch (T_max -> infinity as R -> infinity). One flag, not trained.

inputs: item ids for the batch (B,), used to gather the frozen r_i
level-1 codebook E1 (256 x 32, Euclidean, unchanged)
frozen scalars R, kappa, T_max, b_bar, T_bar and the baseline norm floor eps
batch x, codebooks E_2..E_L, the unchanged decoder and the baseline loss weights
outputs: the Euclidean level-1 code vector e_{k1} (B x 32) used by the straight-through reconstruction
residual res_1 = z - e_{k1} (B x 32) handed unchanged to levels 2..L
codes k_2..k_L, reconstruction x_hat and the scalar baseline loss
frozen tables s_i, T_i (float32, 24556) and scalars b_bar, T_bar, R, kappa, T_max
parameters: frozen float32 tables s_i, T_i (length 24556) and the scalar b_bar, T_bar
R = max(1, log(N_items)/log(1+max(b_bar,1.1))), kappa = -1/R^2, c = 1/R^2, T_max = 2R*atanh(0.95)
the idea's floor constant 1e-6 R^4 is NOT a parameter of the implemented equation (removed, floor case mapped to +inf)
switches: USE_BEHAV (behaviour switch): True uses the frozen per-item T_i = log(1+s_i) as the radius input; False substitutes the catalogue mean T_bar for every item, so all items sit at the single radius R*tanh(min(T_bar,T_max)/(2R)) and the level-1 assignment becomes a common-radius, item-independent metric d_ik = d_c(u,c_k) with no per-item branching resolution (it is not purely angular: the distance still depends on ||c_k|| and, through the eps guard in zhat, on ||z||). Only the lookup changes; R, kappa and T_max are untouched. One flag, not trained in this round.

USE_CURV (geometry switch): True uses kappa = -1/R^2 with u_i = r_i*zhat_i, c_k = rho_k*e_k/max(||e_k||,eps) and d_ik = R*arccosh(1 + 2R^2||u_i-c_k||^2/((R^2-||u_i||^2)(R^2-||c_k||^2))). False uses the kappa->0 limit of the same block, u_i = t_i*zhat_i, c_k = ||e_k||_2*e_k/max(||e_k||_2,eps) and d_ik = ||u_i - c_k||_2: since r_i -> t_i/2 and rho_k -> ||e_k||_2/2, the curved distance tends to 2||(t_i/2)zhat_i - (||e_k||_2/2)ehat_k|| = ||u_i - c_k|| exactly (constant 1, not 2/R and not R/2), so the switch's Euclidean d IS the kappa->0 limit and the common factor 1/2 is what leaves the argmin unchanged. Behaviour still sets a radial offset; the metric is flat. One flag, not trained in this round.
excluded: Sinkhorn / optimal-transport assignment and any soft, entropic or temperature-relaxed matching at any level: the level-1 assignment is a plain argmin by specification, so no solver, no annealing and no clip bound enters.

Curvature, per-item radii, a ball lift or a non-Euclidean distance at levels 2..L: those levels are deliberately exactly the baseline Euclidean argmin, with no interface change; the mechanism is shallow only.

Any extra term in the objective: no behaviour auxiliary loss, no curvature or radius regulariser, no uniformity term, no new hyperparameter; the baseline reconstruction + codebook + commitment loss is used verbatim (adding a term would be a different mechanism).

Any learned or scheduled geometry: R, kappa, c, T_max, T_i, T_bar, b_bar and r_i are precomputed once from the TRAINING split and frozen; no gradient, EMA or optimizer update reaches them, and no count is recomputed from validation/test data.
Training or tuning USE_BEHAV / USE_CURV in this round: both are single fixed flags on the same code path, exercised only as ablations.

The idea's denominator floor max(., 1e-6 R^4) is not implemented: the equation run is the unfloored one and the floor case is mapped to +inf. This is an explicit, argmin-neutral deviation, not a silent drop.

The geometry contract's projection is deliberately omitted for BOTH u_i and c_k: it is a no-op for u_i (r_i <= 0.95R) and is intentionally not applied to c_k, whose norm may approach R; the resulting d_ik = +inf is the intended consequence and such a code is never selected. No 0.999 unit-ball clamp is used anywhere.
Any out/in-degree pair of marginals: the idea defines one item-count vector, and it is used at both indices; no separate column marginal is introduced without explicit sign-off.
Changes to the decoder, to the deeper codebooks, to the straight-through convention or to the Stage-3 input format: unchanged by construction and out of scope.

Riemannian machinery beyond point-to-point distance: no exp/log maps, no Frechet or geodesic means, no hyperbolic attention, no Riemannian optimiser; E1 stays Euclidean and the ball is used only as the level-1 scoring space.
Items with no training-split row: the radius table covers exactly the 24556 training items; unseen items are out of scope.

continuous_surface.name: level1_poincare_distance
continuous_surface.note: The differentiable part, with the radius clamps applied INSIDE the surface: r = R*tanh(min(T,T_max)/(2R)) <= 0.95R < R (T_max = 2R*atanh(0.95) is the same clamp as the idea's T_max) and rho = R*tanh(ne/(2R)) < R, so den > 0 on the whole domain and no floor is needed or present: the floor case den <= 0 (reachable only when rho rounds to R in float64) returns +inf, as the implementation does. Domain and gradcheck: R >= 1, T >= 0, ||x|| > eps, and ne bounded away from the float64 overflow that makes rho == R; the gradcheck stays inside this domain. d = R*acosh(arg) is a positive item-independent rescaling of the idea's literal arccosh(arg), required for d_c(0,u) = 2R*atanh(r/R) = min(T,T_max) and for the flat limit to be 2||u-c||. USE_CURV=False replaces the last block by u = (min(T,T_max)/2)*x/Max(||x||,eps), c = (ne/Max(ne,eps))*e/2, d = 2*sqrt((u0-c0)**2 + (u1-c1)**2); USE_BEHAV=False replaces T by T_bar.
